newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUNESS QUITS SOUTHAMPTON AFTER LESS THAN A YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUNESS QUITS SOUTHAMPTON AFTER LESS THAN A YEAR.

text.p: Graeme Souness resigned as Southampton manager on Saturday, less than a year after joining the English premier league club.
Souness, who joined Southampton last July after being sacked by Turkish club Galatasaray, announced the shock decision through his solicitor in London.
He said in a brief statement: "It is now clear to me that I am not able to take the club forward in the way in which I would like."
The former Scottish international captain is tipped to take over at Italian second division club Torino. He is a former Sampdoria player.
Souness became Southampton manager last July when he was sacked after just one season at Galatasaray despite leading the club to victory in the Turkish Cup final.
He succeeded in keeping Southampton in the premier league, though their safety was secured only on the final day of the season two weeks ago.
Dave Merrington, who was sacked by Southampton only weeks before Souness was brought in, criticised his successor's decision to resign with two years left on his contract.
"The man signed a three-year contract and should have stuck to it," he said. "I can't see why he couldn't have taken the club forward.
"The board had got behind him and given him more money to spend than any other Saints manager in the club's history.
"Southampton gambled a great deal bringing him in -- by doing so they lost their family club image forever.
"Now it just looks as though it's a gamble which went badly wrong."
